title: Reaching Points
statement:
You stand at a point `(a, b)` with positive integer coordinates. In one move you may go from `(x, y)` to either `(x + y, y)` or `(x, x + y)`. You may make any number of moves, including zero.

Decide whether the target point `(c, d)` can be reached from `(a, b)`.
inputFormat: A single line with four integers `a`, `b`, `c`, `d`.
outputFormat: Print `YES` if `(c, d)` is reachable from `(a, b)`, otherwise print `NO`.

examples.explanation: While y stays 4, x can only become 3, 7, 11, ... (add 4 each time). x = 10 is never hit, and changing y would make it larger than 4 forever.
The target equals the start, which needs zero moves.

hints: Going forward every point has two choices, but going backward from (c, d) there is at most one sensible predecessor. Why? Think about which coordinate is larger.
If c > d, the last move must have been (c - d, d) -> (c, d); if d > c, it was (c, d - c) -> (c, d). If c = d there is no valid predecessor.
Subtracting one step at a time can take about 10^9 steps. Replace a whole run of subtractions with a single modulo, but be careful not to jump past the start's coordinates.
